### voxy.refprep.forget(samples, source, \*, run=None, dry_run=False, log=<built-in function print>)

Remove `source`’s clips (only those of one `run`, if given) from a samples
store: its manifest entries, their clip keys and the source’s conditioned key.
Returns the deleted keys (with `dry_run=True`: the keys it would delete, changing
nothing).

With `forget_orphans`, one of the only two functions in voxy that delete voice
samples (`prepare_reference` never does), so it is careful about what it deletes:

- entries match `source` by `source_identity` (real path, in the case the
  filesystem stores it): of their `source_path`, or, for entries an older voxy
  wrote without one, of their `source` only if it is absolute. A relative
  `source` names whatever file had that name where that run started, so such
  entries never match; they are logged, and `run=LEGACY_RUN` removes them
  deliberately (matching `source` exactly as recorded, as in
  `forget(samples, "vocals.wav", run=LEGACY_RUN)`);
- only keys of the form this module writes (`clips/<slug>-NNNN.wav`,
  `conditioned/<slug>.wav`), with a slug taken from a matched entry’s clip key, are
  deleted, never a top-level sample;
- a key a remaining entry names, or whose slug a remaining entry uses, is kept;
- one writer at a time: two processes changing one store at once can lose a
  manifest update (the store has no lock);
- the manifest is read just before it is written, and written first, so an
  interruption leaves unlisted files, never a manifest naming deleted ones.

```pycon
>>> store = {"clips/a-0001.wav": b"A", "conditioned/a.wav": b"C",
...          "clips/b-0001.wav": b"B", "tape1.wav": b"T"}
>>> store[MANIFEST_KEY] = _dump_manifest([
...     {"key": "clips/a-0001.wav", "slug": "a", "source": "/s/a.wav"},
...     {"key": "clips/b-0001.wav", "slug": "b", "source": "/s/b.wav"},
...     {"key": "tape1.wav", "source": "/s/a.wav"}])
>>> forget(store, "/s/a.wav", dry_run=True)
['clips/a-0001.wav', 'conditioned/a.wav']
>>> len(load_manifest(store)), len(store)
(3, 5)
>>> forget(store, "/s/a.wav")
['clips/a-0001.wav', 'conditioned/a.wav']
>>> [e["key"] for e in load_manifest(store)], sorted(store)
(['clips/b-0001.wav'], ['clips/b-0001.wav', 'manifest.jsonl', 'tape1.wav'])
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### voxy.refprep.forget_orphans(samples, , dry_run=True, stale_after=21600)

Delete the `orphans` of a samples store, and the stale pending markers (those
older than `stale_after` seconds); return their keys. A dry run by default: it
returns what it would delete and changes nothing, so look first, then pass
`dry_run=False`.

**Removing entries from the manifest by hand makes their clips orphans**, which
`forget_orphans` then deletes, even if a saved voice profile’s `ref_audio` still
points at one. To drop a source’s clips, use `forget` (it lists, with
`dry_run=True`, exactly what it removes), never a hand edit of the manifest.

With `forget`, one of the only two functions in voxy that delete voice samples.
It refuses (raises, deleting nothing) where `orphans` does: a missing or empty
manifest beside unclaimed clip or conditioned keys, a manifest or pending marker it
cannot read. Keys a running `prepare_reference` reserved (its live marker) are
kept, but a run that is still going after `stale_after` seconds loses that claim.

```pycon
>>> store = {"conditioned/z.wav": b"", "clips/a-0001.wav": b"", "tape1.wav": b""}
>>> store[MANIFEST_KEY] = _dump_manifest([{"key": "clips/a-0001.wav"}])
>>> forget_orphans(store), sorted(store)
(['conditioned/z.wav'], ['clips/a-0001.wav', 'conditioned/z.wav', 'manifest.jsonl', 'tape1.wav'])
>>> forget_orphans(store, dry_run=False), sorted(store)
(['conditioned/z.wav'], ['clips/a-0001.wav', 'manifest.jsonl', 'tape1.wav'])
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### voxy.refprep.latest_runs(manifest)

`manifest` with, per source, only the entries of its most recent run.

`prepare_reference` keeps every run, so a source processed twice is in the
manifest twice (the same audio, cut again); consumers that want one copy of each
recording (training sets, reference picks, summaries) read this. Sources are told
apart by `source_identity` (of `source_path`, or an absolute `source`), so one
file recorded in two spellings on a case-insensitive filesystem is one source;
entries with no `run` count as one run older than any recorded one; entries whose
source cannot be known (none, or a relative path from an older voxy) are all kept.
Order is kept. A source whose newest run gave no clips keeps its older run’s
entries.

```pycon
>>> m = [{"key": "a1", "source_path": "/a", "run": "20260101T000000.000000Z-x"},
...      {"key": "a2", "source_path": "/a", "run": "20261101T000000.000000Z-y"},
...      {"key": "a0", "source_path": "/a"},
...      {"key": "b1", "source_path": "/b"},
...      {"key": "t", "source": "tape.wav"}]
>>> [e["key"] for e in latest_runs(m)]
['a2', 'b1', 't']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]

### voxy.refprep.load_manifest(samples)

The manifest saved by `prepare_reference` in a samples store.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.refprep.orphans(samples, , stale_after=21600)

The keys of this module’s own form (`clips/<slug>-NNNN.wav`,
`conditioned/<slug>.wav`) whose slug no manifest entry and no live pending marker
uses, sorted.

**Removing entries from the manifest by hand makes their clips orphans**, which
`forget_orphans` then deletes, even if a saved voice profile’s `ref_audio` still
points at one. To drop a source’s clips, use `forget` (it lists, with
`dry_run=True`, exactly what it removes), never a hand edit of the manifest.

Where they come from: a run that failed part-way (the failing source’s conditioned
file and any clips it had cut), a source that gave no clips (its conditioned file),
a manifest edited by hand. `prepare_reference` never reuses their slugs and
`forget` never deletes them, since no entry names them. A key an entry names is
never an orphan (its slug is that entry’s), nor is any other key (a top-level
sample, the manifest). A running `prepare_reference` claims its slugs with a
pending marker (`PENDING_PREFIX`), so its keys not in the manifest yet are not
orphans; a marker older than `stale_after` seconds (a crashed run’s) claims
nothing.

It raises, rather than guess, when the manifest has a line that is not an object,
when a pending marker cannot be read, and when the manifest is missing or empty
while keys of this module’s form are unclaimed (a lost or truncated manifest would
otherwise make every clip an orphan).

```pycon
>>> store = {"clips/a-0001.wav": b"", "clips/x-0001.wav": b"", "conditioned/a.wav": b"",
...          "conditioned/z.wav": b"", "tape1.wav": b""}
>>> store[MANIFEST_KEY] = _dump_manifest([{"key": "clips/a-0001.wav", "slug": "a"}])
>>> orphans(store)
['clips/x-0001.wav', 'conditioned/z.wav']
>>> store["pending/r.json"] = _pending_marker("r", ["x"])  # a run is cutting x
>>> orphans(store), orphans(store, stale_after=0)
(['conditioned/z.wav'], ['clips/x-0001.wav', 'conditioned/z.wav'])
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### voxy.refprep.partial_transcribe(rootdir=None)

The default transcriber, bound to a data root.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]]

### voxy.refprep.plan_clips(segments, , min_seconds=3.0, max_seconds=12.0, pad_seconds=0.12, total_seconds=None)

Clips `[{start, end, text, words}]` cut between words, ending sentences where possible.

Words accumulate until the clip passes `min_seconds` and a word ends a
sentence (or the next word would push it past `max_seconds`). Cuts fall in
the pause between two words, padded by up to `pad_seconds`. A word marked
`keep=False` (someone else’s, see `voxy.speakers`) ends the clip before it,
and the next clip starts after it.

```pycon
>>> w = lambda s, e, t: {"start": s, "end": e, "text": t, "confidence": 0.9}
>>> segs = [{"words": [w(0, 1, "One"), w(1.1, 2, "two."), w(3, 4, "Three"),
...                    w(4.1, 5, "four.")], "start": 0, "end": 5, "text": ""}]
>>> [c["text"] for c in plan_clips(segs, min_seconds=1.5, max_seconds=3)]
['One two.', 'Three four.']
>>> segs[0]["words"].insert(2, {**w(2.2, 2.6, " yes"), "keep": False})
>>> [(c["text"], c["start"]) for c in plan_clips(segs, min_seconds=1.5, max_seconds=3)]
[('One two.', 0.0), ('Three four.', 2.88)]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.refprep.prepare_reference(sources, \*, voice=None, samples=None, sample_rate=24000, denoise='afftdn', loudness_lufs=-20.0, min_seconds=3.0, max_seconds=12.0, language=None, transcriber=None, conditioner=None, speaker=None, rootdir=None, log=<built-in function print>)

Condition, transcribe, cut and score `sources`; save clips and manifest; return it.

* **Parameters:**
  * **sources** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)]) – Recordings, any format ffmpeg reads.
  * **voice** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Voice name: clips go to `samples_store(voice)`.
  * **samples** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A store to write to instead (`filename -> bytes`).
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Conditioning (see `condition`).
  * **denoise** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Conditioning (see `condition`).
  * **loudness_lufs** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Conditioning (see `condition`).
  * **min_seconds** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Clip length bounds.
  * **max_seconds** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Clip length bounds.
  * **language** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Force the ASR language (default: detected).
  * **transcriber** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(wav_path, language=) -> segments` (default `transcribe`).
  * **conditioner** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(src, dst, sample_rate=, filters=) -> path` (default `condition`).
  * **speaker** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(wav_path, segments) -> segments` marking other voices’ words
    (`voxy.speakers.speaker_filter`); None keeps every voice.
* **Returns:**
  one dict per clip (`key`, `path` if on disk, `text`,
  `source` as given, `source_path` (its `source_identity`), `slug`,
  `run` (one id per call), `start`, `end`, and the `score_clip`
  measures), best first, earlier runs’ entries included.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

It never deletes or overwrites anything in the store. Run again into the same store
(another recording, or the same file again), it gives this run’s sources fresh slugs
that no manifest entry and no clip or conditioned key in the store already uses, so
every earlier clip keeps its key and its bytes, and saved reference profiles
(`ref_audio` + `ref_text`) stay valid. The manifest keeps every earlier entry and
gets each source’s new ones as soon as that source is done (re-read just before
each write, so a `forget` or another run that finished meanwhile is not undone):
a run that fails part-way leaves its finished sources recorded, and only the
failing source’s keys (its conditioned file, any clips already cut) in no manifest,
which `orphans` lists and `forget_orphans` removes. Re-processing a source
therefore adds clips beside its earlier ones; consumers read
`latest_runs(manifest)` to see one run per source, and
`forget(samples, source, run=...)` removes the others explicitly. A file given
twice in one call (by `source_identity`) is processed once. While it runs, a
pending marker (`pending/<run>.json`: run id, start time, reserved slugs) keeps
`forget_orphans` off its keys; it is removed when the run finishes, and a crashed
run’s marker stays (showing the crash) until it is stale (`PENDING_STALE_S`).

### voxy.refprep.score_clip(samples, sample_rate, , words=(), text='', min_seconds=3.0, max_seconds=12.0)

Quality measures of a clip, and their combination `score` in [0, 1].

- `snr_db`: loud-frame level minus quiet-frame level (speech vs floor).
- `clipped`: fraction of samples at full scale.
- `level_db`: level of the loud frames.
- `asr_confidence`: mean Whisper word probability (low: mumbling, noise, music).
- `chars_per_second`: speaking rate (outliers: bad alignment).
- `speaker_similarity`: lowest match of a word to the target voice (words
  annotated by `voxy.speakers`; None otherwise).

```pycon
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
>>> speechy = np.concatenate([0.3 * rng.standard_normal(40000), 0.001 * rng.standard_normal(8000)])
>>> s = score_clip(speechy, 8000, text="x" * 70)
>>> s["snr_db"] > 30, 0 < s["score"] <= 1
(True, True)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### voxy.refprep.source_identity(source)

What tells sources apart: the real path (so a relative and an absolute path, or
a symlink, to one file are one source), spelled as the filesystem stores it when
the file exists (so `Talk.wav` and `talk.wav` typed for one file on a
case-insensitive filesystem are one source), then in Unicode normal form
`UNICODE_FORM` (so an NFC and an NFD spelling of `Café.wav` are one source), then
`os.path.normcase`. A file that does not exist (any more) falls back to its real
path as typed.

```pycon
>>> source_identity("/no/such/Dir/a.wav") == os.path.normcase(
...     os.path.realpath("/no/such/Dir/a.wav"))
True
>>> source_identity("/no/Cafe\u0301.wav") == source_identity("/no/Caf\u00e9.wav")
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.refprep.summarize(manifest)

Totals for a manifest: clips, minutes, minutes above score thresholds.

```pycon
>>> summarize([{"duration": 60, "score": 0.9}, {"duration": 30, "score": 0.4}])
{'clips': 2, 'minutes': 1.5, 'minutes_score_0.5+': 1.0, 'minutes_score_0.7+': 1.0}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### voxy.refprep.transcribe(audio, , language=None, model='large-v3-turbo', threads=None, rootdir=None)

Timed segments `[{start, end, text, confidence, words: [...]}, ...]` of `audio`.

### voxy.refprep.transcribe_text(audio, \*\*kwargs)

The transcript of `audio` as one string.

### voxy.refprep.unique_slugs(sources, , reserved=())

One distinct slug per source: the file’s stem, plus parent folders only within a
group of sources sharing a stem (stem tracks: every one is `vocals.wav`), numbered
where folders cannot tell them apart. Slugs never climb past what separates a group,
and a source whose stem is unique keeps it.

```pycon
>>> unique_slugs(["/s/one/vocals.wav", "/s/two/vocals.wav", "/s/talk.m4a"])
['one-vocals', 'two-vocals', 'talk']
>>> unique_slugs(["/Users/x/audio/talk.m4a", "/Users/x/audio/talk.wav"])
['talk', 'talk-2']
>>> unique_slugs(["/s/a.wav", "/s/a.wav", "/s/a-2.wav"])
['a', 'a-3', 'a-2']
```

`reserved` slugs (already used in the store) are never given out:

```pycon
>>> unique_slugs(["/t/vocals.wav"], reserved=["vocals"])
['vocals-2']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### voxy.refprep.with_deepfilternet(conditioner=None, , denoiser=None, rootdir=None)

A `conditioner` that denoises with DeepFilterNet between two ffmpeg passes.

Pass 1 converts the source to a 48 kHz mono WAV (no filters); DeepFilterNet cleans
it; pass 2 applies the usual `filters` (high-pass, loudness) and resamples to
`sample_rate`. `conditioner` (default [`condition()`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.condition)) does both ffmpeg passes.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)]

# voxy.say_model

Local speech with the macOS `say` command: free, offline, no API key, no deps.

Good for previews and drafts before spending credits on a cloud voice. Voices are
the system’s (`say -v '?'`): e.g. “Samantha”, “Daniel”, “Karen”.

```pycon
>>> SaySpeechModel(run=lambda *a, **k: None).dflt_voice
```

# _autosummary/voxy.score.html.md

# voxy.score

Scores for singing: the notes of a melody (pitch, timing, word) from MIDI, MusicXML
or plain code, with lyrics attached.

A `Note` is one sung note in absolute seconds: its MIDI pitch, the word sung on it,
and whether the word starts on it (`starts_word`) or continues from the note
before (a melisma, or the later syllables of a word). Rests are the gaps between
notes. A singing backend turns a list of notes into its own input format
(`voxy.soulx.soulx_metadata` for SoulX-Singer).

```pycon
>>> from voxy.score import read_score
>>> notes = read_score("melody.mid", "Light a can-dle in the win-dow")
>>> notes = read_score("song.musicxml")         # the score's own lyrics
```

Lyrics are a line of whitespace-separated tokens, one per sung note:
`can-dle` spreads one word over two notes, a bare `-` (or `_`) holds the
previous word one more note.

```pycon
>>> notes = notes_from_pitches([(64, 1), (67, 1), (60, 2)], bpm=120)
>>> [(n.start, n.dur, n.pitch) for n in notes]
[(0.0, 0.5, 64), (0.5, 0.5, 67), (1.0, 1.0, 60)]
>>> [(n.word, n.starts_word) for n in attach_lyrics(notes, "hel-lo you")]
[('hello', True), ('hello', False), ('you', True)]
```

MIDI is read with `mido` (every tempo change honoured, lyric meta-events kept),
MusicXML (and anything else music21 parses) with `music21`: both are in the
`voxy[singing]` extra and imported only when a score of that kind is read.

### Module Attributes

| [`HOLD_TOKENS`](_autosummary/voxy.score.html.md#voxy.score.HOLD_TOKENS)        | Tokens of a lyric line that hold the previous word one more note.                             |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_FILLER_WORD`](_autosummary/voxy.score.html.md#voxy.score.DFLT_FILLER_WORD)   | The word given to sung notes that have none (a score without lyrics on every note).           |
| [`DFLT_MIDI_TEMPO`](_autosummary/voxy.score.html.md#voxy.score.DFLT_MIDI_TEMPO)    | 500 000 microseconds a beat (120 BPM).                                                        |
| [`DRUM_CHANNEL`](_autosummary/voxy.score.html.md#voxy.score.DRUM_CHANNEL)       | percussion, never a melody.                                                                   |
| [`DFLT_MAX_OVERLAP_S`](_autosummary/voxy.score.html.md#voxy.score.DFLT_MAX_OVERLAP_S) | A note may overlap the next by this much (legato) before the line counts as polyphonic.       |
| [`WORD_BREAK_REST_S`](_autosummary/voxy.score.html.md#voxy.score.WORD_BREAK_REST_S)  | a note after it without a lyric of its own starts a new word instead of continuing (melisma). |

* **Type:**
  MIDI tempo before any `set_tempo` event

### voxy.score.DRUM_CHANNEL *= 9*

percussion, never a melody.

* **Type:**
  MIDI channel 10 (index 9)

### voxy.score.HOLD_TOKENS *= frozenset({'-', '_'})*

Tokens of a lyric line that hold the previous word one more note.

### *class* voxy.score.Note(start, dur, pitch, word='', starts_word=True)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One sung note, in absolute seconds.

* **Parameters:**
  * **start** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Onset (seconds from the start of the score).
  * **dur** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Duration in seconds.
  * **pitch** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – MIDI note number (60 is middle C).
  * **word** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The word sung on it (’’ until lyrics are attached).
  * **starts_word** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – True if the word starts here; False if it continues the
    previous note’s word (melisma, later syllable).

#### *property* end *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

Where the note stops (seconds).

### voxy.score.WORD_BREAK_REST_S *= 0.2*

a note after it without a lyric of
its own starts a new word instead of continuing (melisma).

* **Type:**
  A gap this long between notes ends a word

### voxy.score.attach_lyrics(notes, lyrics)

`notes` with the words of `lyrics` (see `lyric_tokens`), one token per note.

```pycon
>>> attach_lyrics(notes_from_pitches([(60, 1)]), "two words")
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ValueError: 2 lyric syllables for 1 notes: write 'can-dle' for one word over two notes, '-' to hold a word
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Note`](_autosummary/voxy.score.html.md#voxy.score.Note)]

### voxy.score.lyric_tokens(lyrics)

`(word, starts_word)` per sung note, from a lyric line.

```pycon
>>> lyric_tokens("Light a can-dle - in")
[('Light', True), ('a', True), ('candle', True), ('candle', False), ('candle', False), ('in', True)]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)]]

### voxy.score.notes_from_midi(path, , track=None, channel=None, max_overlap_s=0.1, with_lyrics=True)

The melody of a MIDI file: the notes of one track and channel, with its lyric
events joined into words.

The line is the one track and channel that has notes, drums (channel 10) aside;
with several, pass `track=` (its index in the file) and, for a file that mixes
channels in one track, `channel=` (1 to 16); the error lists the candidates.
Times follow the file’s tempo map. A note overlapping the next by up to
`max_overlap_s` (legato) is cut at the next onset; more, or two notes starting
together, is polyphony, and an error.

Words come from `lyrics` meta-events only (never `text` events, so a label
is never sung), on the melody’s track, else on the one other track that has
them (type-1 files often keep them in track 0). Each is a syllable on the note
sounding at its tick (from a little before its onset to its end); one that
falls on no note, or a second one on a note, is an error. A trailing `-`
(`can-`) or a leading one (`-dle`) joins syllables into one word; a note
without a syllable continues the word before it (a melisma), unless a rest
separates them. `with_lyrics=False` reads no lyrics (words come from
elsewhere). Karaoke files (`.kar`, lyrics in `text` events) are not
supported yet: full score reading is planned in audiate
([https://github.com/thorwhalen/audiate/issues/2](https://github.com/thorwhalen/audiate/issues/2)).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Note`](_autosummary/voxy.score.html.md#voxy.score.Note)]

### voxy.score.notes_from_musicxml(score, , part=0)

The notes of one part of a MusicXML file (or any score music21 reads, or a
music21 stream), with its lyrics as words.

Only the part’s first voice is read (timed by the part’s own tempo marks), and
only its first verse of lyrics; grace notes and zero-length notes are skipped;
a chord sings its highest note. Tied notes become one. Syllables are
joined into words with MusicXML’s `syllabic` (begin, middle, end), so
`can-dle` on two notes is `candle` on both, the second continuing the
word. A note without a lyric continues the word before it (a melisma under a
slur), unless a rest came between.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Note`](_autosummary/voxy.score.html.md#voxy.score.Note)]

### voxy.score.notes_from_pitches(pitches, , bpm=100, start=0.0)

Notes from `(midi_pitch, beats)` pairs, back to back; a pitch of 0 or None is a rest.

```pycon
>>> [(n.start, n.pitch) for n in notes_from_pitches([(60, 1), (0, 1), (62, 1)], bpm=60)]
[(0.0, 60), (2.0, 62)]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Note`](_autosummary/voxy.score.html.md#voxy.score.Note)]

### voxy.score.read_score(score, lyrics=None, , filler='la', track=None, channel=None, part=0)

The notes of `score`, with words: from `lyrics` if given, else the score’s own.

* **Parameters:**
  * **score** – A MIDI file (`.mid`, `.midi`), a MusicXML file (`.musicxml`,
    `.xml`, `.mxl`, or anything music21 parses), a music21 stream, or
    a sequence of `Note`.
  * **lyrics** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A lyric line (one token per note, see `lyric_tokens`); replaces
    the score’s own words.
  * **filler** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The word for sung notes that still have none and continue no word
    (a note after a rest, in a score with lyrics on only some notes); a
    score with no words at all, and no `lyrics`, is an error.
  * **track** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The MIDI line to sing (see `notes_from_midi`).
  * **channel** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The MIDI line to sing (see `notes_from_midi`).
  * **part** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – The MusicXML part to sing.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Note`](_autosummary/voxy.score.html.md#voxy.score.Note)]

```pycon
>>> [n.word for n in read_score(notes_from_pitches([(60, 1), (62, 1)]), "do re")]
['do', 're']
```


# _autosummary/voxy.script.html.md

# voxy.script

Render a cast script: text segments, each read by its own voice, one audio file per section.

For anything narrated by more than one voice (an audiobook with a narrator and a quoted
guide, a dialogue, a radio play). Three plain-data inputs, each a JSON-able mapping so a
person can edit them and the rest follows:

- the **script**: a list of sections `{"id", "title"?, "segments": [{"role", "text"}]}`;
- the **casting**: `{"roles": {role: voice name or None}, "takes": {section id: take},
  "default_role"?}`; a role mapped to `None` has no voice yet (its sections are listed,
  not rendered);
- the **voices**: voice name -> `{"backend"?, "init"?, "params"?, "tempo"?, "effect"?,
  "external"?}` plus how to load it (`"library": name`, `"reference": {"audio", "text"}`
  or `"voice": id-or-name` passed to the backend as is). `tempo` (pitch kept, rubberband)
  and `effect` (an ffmpeg audio filter) are finishing steps; `external` marks a voice
  synthesised elsewhere (`missing_takes` lists what it owes, `add_take` files the audio).

Files under `root`:

> segments/<key>.wav|json   one take of one segment; the key hashes (voice, settings,
> : spoken text, take number), so a take is never overwritten
>   and an edit makes a new one

> sections/<id>.mp3         a section’s takes joined: pauses, tempo, effect, loudness
> : (EBU R128) evened across voices, a gap where the voice changes

> index.json                per section: status, segments (key, role, voice), file, seconds

Render again after editing: only segments whose key changed are synthesised, and only
sections whose takes or finishing changed are rebuilt. A retake of a section is
`"takes": {"s1": 2}` in the casting (a `seed` in the voice’s params moves with the take).

```pycon
>>> script = [{"id": "s1", "segments": [{"role": "guide", "text": "Come."}, {"role": "author", "text": "I come."}]}]
>>> casting = {"roles": {"guide": "g", "author": "a"}}
>>> [(s["role"], s["voice"]) for s in plan_script(script, casting)[0]["segments"]]
[('guide', 'g'), ('author', 'a')]
```

### Functions

| [`add_take`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.add_take)(root, segment, audio, \*[, ...])       | File one take: `segments/<key>.wav` (`audio`: WAV bytes) and its `.json`.                           |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`finish_section`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.finish_section)(wavs, out, finish)               | Join takes (each `(wav path, voice spec)`) into one MP3 at `out`.                                   |
| [`lengthen_pauses`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.lengthen_pauses)(samples, sr, \*, tiers[, ...])  | `samples` (mono float array) with each inner pause lengthened by its tier's extra seconds.          |
| [`load_voice_profile`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.load_voice_profile)(spec, \*[, root])            | The voice to hand `synthesize` from a voices entry (see the module docstring).                      |
| [`missing_takes`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.missing_takes)(script, root, \*[, casting, ...]) | Segments with no take yet (by default only those of external voices), in script order.              |
| [`plan_script`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.plan_script)(script, casting, \*[, text_prep])   | Each section with its segments resolved: `{role, voice, text, tts_text, take}`.                     |
| [`render_script`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.render_script)(script, root, \*[, casting, ...]) | Render what is missing or changed, section by section in script order; return (and save) the index. |
| [`segment_key`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.segment_key)(segment, voice)                     | A take's identity: a hash of the voice (loading and settings), spoken text and take number.         |
| [`status`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.status)(root)                                    | Progress from `index.json`: counts per status, total `seconds`, `segments_by_voice`.                |

### voxy.script.add_take(root, segment, audio, , generation_seconds=None)

File one take: `segments/<key>.wav` (`audio`: WAV bytes) and its `.json`.

`segment` is an entry of `missing_takes` (or the renderer’s own), with `key` and
`voice_spec`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### voxy.script.finish_section(wavs, out, finish)

Join takes (each `(wav path, voice spec)`) into one MP3 at `out`.

Per take: pauses, then tempo, effect and loudness; a silent gap follows each take but
the last. Needs `ffmpeg` (with rubberband for `tempo`).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### voxy.script.lengthen_pauses(samples, sr, , tiers, floor_db=-35.0)

`samples` (mono float array) with each inner pause lengthened by its tier’s extra seconds.

A pause is a run of 10 ms frames `floor_db` below the loud frames (95th percentile);
it is lengthened by repeating its own middle, so the room tone carries on. Leading and
trailing silence is left as is.

```pycon
>>> tone = np.sin(np.arange(8000) / 3.0).astype(np.float32)
>>> y = np.concatenate([tone, np.zeros(4000, np.float32), tone])  # 0.5 s pause at 8 kHz
>>> len(lengthen_pauses(y, 8000, tiers=[[0.4, 0.25]])) - len(y)
2000
```

### voxy.script.load_voice_profile(spec, , root=None)

The voice to hand `synthesize` from a voices entry (see the module docstring).

### voxy.script.missing_takes(script, root, , casting=None, voices=None, text_prep=None, external_only=True)

Segments with no take yet (by default only those of external voices), in script order.

Each is `{section, role, voice, text, tts_text, take, key, voice_spec}`: hand it to
whatever renders that voice, then file the audio with `add_take(root, segment, wav)`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.script.plan_script(script, casting, , text_prep=None)

Each section with its segments resolved: `{role, voice, text, tts_text, take}`.

`tts_text` is `text_prep(text)` (what is spoken; default: the text itself), so the
take’s key follows what the voice says, not the displayed text.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.script.render_script(script, root, \*, casting=None, voices=None, only=None, finish=None, text_prep=None, model_factory=None, voice_loader=<function load_voice_profile>, log=<built-in function print>)

Render what is missing or changed, section by section in script order; return (and save) the index.

* **Parameters:**
  * **script** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]) – Sections `{"id", "title"?, "segments": [{"role", "text"}]}`.
  * **root** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)) – The output folder; `casting` and `voices` default to its
    `casting.json` and `voices.json`.
  * **only** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Section ids to render (default all); the index still lists every section.
  * **finish** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Overrides of `DFLT_FINISH` (gap between voices, loudness, bitrate, pauses).
  * **text_prep** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `text -> spoken text` per segment (e.g. `voxy.speechtext` preparation).
  * **model_factory** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(backend, **init) -> SpeechModel` (default `voxy.create_speech_model`).
  * **voice_loader** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)) – `(voice spec, root=) -> voice` (default `load_voice_profile`).
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### voxy.script.segment_key(segment, voice)

A take’s identity: a hash of the voice (loading and settings), spoken text and take number.

`tempo` and `effect` are finishing steps, left out: changing them rebuilds the
section files without new takes.

```pycon
>>> a = segment_key({"tts_text": "Hi", "take": 1}, {"params": {"seed": 1}})
>>> a == segment_key({"tts_text": "Hi", "take": 1}, {"params": {"seed": 1}, "tempo": 0.8})
True
>>> a == segment_key({"tts_text": "Hi", "take": 2}, {"params": {"seed": 1}})
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.script.status(root)

Progress from `index.json`: counts per status, total `seconds`, `segments_by_voice`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/voxy.separate.html.md

# voxy.separate

Split a recording into the voice and the rest (music, noise) before using the voice.

A song or a noisy interview has to lose its backing before its voice can be cloned,
transcribed or edited. `separate` runs Demucs (MIT; `htdemucs_ft` by default, the
fine-tuned hybrid transformer) in its own environment, built on first use under the
data root like the other local models, and returns the two stems as WAV bytes:
the voice, and `rest`, the input minus the voice (so the two add back up to it).

```pycon
>>> from voxy.separate import separate
>>> stems = separate("song.mp3")
>>> open("vocals.wav", "wb").write(stems["vocals"])
```

`run` is the seam (`(audio_path, out_dir, *, stem, sample_rate, \*\*options) ->
{stem: path}`); tests and other separators plug in there.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, pathlib
>>> def fake(audio, out_dir, **options):
...     paths = {n: pathlib.Path(out_dir) / f"{n}.wav" for n in ("vocals", "rest")}
...     for p in paths.values():
...         p.write_bytes(b"RIFF")
...     return paths
>>> sorted(separate(b"RIFF....", run=fake))
['rest', 'vocals']
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_STEM`](_autosummary/voxy.separate.html.md#voxy.separate.DFLT_STEM)      | The stem kept as "the voice"; Demucs also has drums, bass and other.            |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`FLOAT_SUBTYPE`](_autosummary/voxy.separate.html.md#voxy.separate.FLOAT_SUBTYPE)  | float, so no level is lost.                                                     |
| [`MODEL_SOURCES`](_autosummary/voxy.separate.html.md#voxy.separate.MODEL_SOURCES)  | The stems of the pretrained models whose sources are known before loading them. |
| [`SEPARATION_ENV`](_autosummary/voxy.separate.html.md#voxy.separate.SEPARATION_ENV) | torch is bounded to the releases Demucs 4.0.1 was checked with.                 |

### Functions

| [`check_stem`](_autosummary/voxy.separate.html.md#voxy.separate.check_stem)(stem, model)                       | Raise `ValueError` if `model` is known (`MODEL_SOURCES`) and lacks `stem`.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`close_separation`](_autosummary/voxy.separate.html.md#voxy.separate.close_separation)()                            | Stop the Demucs workers (free their memory).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`separate`](_autosummary/voxy.separate.html.md#voxy.separate.separate)(audio, \*[, stem, sample_rate, run]) | `{stem: wav, "rest": wav}`: `audio` split into `stem` and everything else.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`speech_separator`](_autosummary/voxy.separate.html.md#voxy.separate.speech_separator)(\*[, stem, run])             | `separate` as a `(samples (frames, channels), sample_rate) -> (speech, music)` callable, the separator seam of reeleehq/mixing (`mixing.audio.separation.separate_speech(audio, separator=speech_separator())`), so mixing can run Demucs out of process, in voxy's environment. |
| [`worker_run`](_autosummary/voxy.separate.html.md#voxy.separate.worker_run)(\*[, model, threads, rootdir])     | The default `run`: the Demucs adapter in its own environment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### voxy.separate.DFLT_STEM *= 'vocals'*

The stem kept as “the voice”; Demucs also has drums, bass and other.

### voxy.separate.FLOAT_SUBTYPE *= 'FLOAT'*

float, so no level is lost.

* **Type:**
  What `speech_separator` asks the worker to write

### voxy.separate.MODEL_SOURCES *= {'htdemucs': ('drums', 'bass', 'other', 'vocals'), 'htdemucs_6s': ('drums', 'bass', 'other', 'vocals', 'guitar', 'piano'), 'htdemucs_ft': ('drums', 'bass', 'other', 'vocals')}*

The stems of the pretrained models whose sources are known before loading them.

### voxy.separate.SEPARATION_ENV *= EnvSpec(name='demucs', requirements=('demucs==4.0.1', 'torch>=2.11,<2.16', 'soundfile', 'numpy'), python='3.11', torch_backend='cpu', env_vars={'TORCH_HOME': '{models}'})*

torch is bounded to the releases Demucs 4.0.1 was checked with. torchaudio comes in
as a Demucs dependency, unpinned: Demucs imports it but never calls it here.

### voxy.separate.check_stem(stem, model)

Raise `ValueError` if `model` is known (`MODEL_SOURCES`) and lacks `stem`.

```pycon
>>> check_stem("vocals", "htdemucs_ft")
>>> check_stem("guitar", "htdemucs_ft")
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ValueError: 'guitar' is not a stem of htdemucs_ft: ['drums', 'bass', 'other', 'vocals']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### voxy.separate.close_separation()

Stop the Demucs workers (free their memory).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### voxy.separate.separate(audio, , stem='vocals', sample_rate=None, run=None, \*\*options)

`{stem: wav, "rest": wav}`: `audio` split into `stem` and everything else.

`rest` is the input minus the voice, so `stem + rest` rebuilds the input (as
the model hears it: resampled and with its channels). Both are 16-bit PCM WAV
with the model’s channels (Demucs: stereo; a mono input is duplicated, the first
two channels of a wider one are kept) at the model’s rate (Demucs: 44.1 kHz)
unless `sample_rate` says otherwise, whatever the input. If either stem would
clip, both are divided by one common factor (Demucs’s `prevent_clip`), so they
still add up to the input times that factor.

The whole file is decoded and held in memory, and Demucs takes about 24 s per
minute of audio on CPU for one model (`htdemucs_ft` runs only the sub-model
fine-tuned for `stem`); split hours-long recordings first.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)) – A path to any format soundfile reads (WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3 with a
    recent libsndfile), or WAV bytes.
  * **stem** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The stem to keep apart (`"vocals"`; Demucs also has drums, bass,
    other).
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The rate of the returned WAVs (default: the model’s).
  * **run** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(audio_path, out_dir, *, stem, sample_rate, \*\*options) ->
    {stem: path}`; default `worker_run()` (Demucs `htdemucs_ft` on CPU).
  * **\*\*options** – Passed to `run` (Demucs: `shifts`, `overlap`).
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)]

### voxy.separate.speech_separator(, stem='vocals', run=None, \*\*options)

`separate` as a `(samples (frames, channels), sample_rate) -> (speech, music)`
callable, the separator seam of reeleehq/mixing
(`mixing.audio.separation.separate_speech(audio, separator=speech_separator())`),
so mixing can run Demucs out of process, in voxy’s environment.

Mono or stereo in; the stems come back at the input’s rate, channels and length,
at the input’s level (no clip rescaling, float WAV in between: `speech + music`
is the input). Keyword arguments are `separate`’s. For mixing’s `remove_talk`,
give it htdemucs’s context: `SeparationStrategy(..., context_s=3.0)` around this
callable (a bare callable gets mixing’s 1 s default).

```pycon
>>> def fake(audio, out_dir, *, stem, sample_rate, **options):
...     samples, sr = read_wav_channels(audio)
...     paths = {}
...     for name, part in ((stem, samples * 0.75), ("rest", samples * 0.25)):
...         paths[name] = f"{out_dir}/{name}.wav"
...         open(paths[name], "wb").write(write_wav_channels(part, sr))
...     return paths
>>> speech, music = speech_separator(run=fake)(np.ones((4, 2)), 8000)
>>> speech.shape, float(speech[0, 0]), float(music[0, 1])
((4, 2), 0.75, 0.25)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, `ndarray`]]

### voxy.separate.worker_run(, model='htdemucs_ft', threads=None, rootdir=None)

The default `run`: the Demucs adapter in its own environment.

A stem the model lacks fails before the worker starts for the models in
`MODEL_SOURCES`, and inside the worker (a `WorkerError` carrying the same
message) for the others.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]


# _autosummary/voxy.singing.html.md

# voxy.singing

Singing: sing a score with lyrics in a voice (SVS), or re-voice a sung take (SVC).

```pycon
>>> import voxy
>>> voxy.sing("melody.mid", "Light a can-dle in the win-dow").save("sung.wav")
>>> voice = voxy.singing_voice("me.wav", "phrase.mid", "la la la la")
>>> voxy.sing("song.musicxml", voice=voice).save("song.wav")
>>> voxy.convert_singing("take.wav", voice=voice).save("take-in-my-voice.wav")
```

A singing *voice* is a sung clip, plus, for synthesis, the notes and words it sings
(`singing_voice`): a zero-shot singer copies the clip’s timbre, and SoulX-Singer
also aligns the clip with its notes and phonemes. The simplest way to get that
alignment is to make the clip from a known score: sing a short given phrase (its
MIDI or MusicXML, with its lyrics) and pass the recording with that score. Without
a voice, a synthetic one is used (`synthetic_singing_voice`: a formant
synthesiser singing “la”, which belongs to no one). Conversion needs only the clip.
Only clone a singing voice with its owner’s consent; each backend records its own
usage restrictions in `singing_backends()[name].consent`.

Scores are MIDI or MusicXML files, music21 streams, or lists of `voxy.score.Note`
(`voxy.score.read_score`); lyrics are one token per note (`can-dle` spreads a
word over two notes, `-` holds it one more).

Backends are `SingingBackend` records (`singing_backends()`), each running in
its own environment (`python -m voxy setup soulx`); `soulx` (SoulX-Singer,
Apache-2.0) is the built-in one. A model is the seam: `sing(..., model=...)`
takes any object with `sing(notes, voice, *, transpose, language, **params)` and
`convert(audio_path, voice, *, transpose, **params)` returning a `Speech`.

```pycon
>>> class Echo:
...     name = "echo"
...     def sing(self, notes, voice, **kw):
...         return Speech(b"RIFF", "wav", "echo", text=" ".join(n.word for n in notes))
>>> from voxy.score import notes_from_pitches
>>> sing(notes_from_pitches([(60, 1), (62, 1)]), "do re", voice=VoiceProfile(
...     {"prompt_audio": "v.wav", "prompt_notes": []}, 0, "echo", 24000), model=Echo()).text
'do re'
```

# _autosummary/voxy.soulx.html.md

# voxy.soulx

SoulX-Singer (Soul AI Lab, 2026; code and weights Apache-2.0): zero-shot singing
voice synthesis and conversion, as the `soulx` singing backend.

```pycon
>>> import voxy
>>> voxy.sing("melody.mid", "Light a can-dle in the win-dow", backend="soulx")
```

How it runs: in its own environment (`python -m voxy setup soulx`: Python 3.11,
torch 2.2, transformers 4.41, the upstream pins). SoulX-Singer has no
`pyproject.toml`, so pip can’t install it: voxy fetches its repository at a pinned
commit (`SOULX_SOURCE`) into `models/soulx/source/<commit>` on first use, and the
adapter puts that folder on `sys.path`. Weights (two 2.8 GB checkpoints, SVS and
SVC, plus RMVPE for F0) come from the Hugging Face Hub at pinned revisions; SVC also
loads `openai/whisper-base` (Apache-2.0) on first use. On Apple Silicon it runs on
MPS, with the vocoder on the CPU; elsewhere on CUDA or the CPU (about 8x real time).

What it reads: SoulX metadata, a list of *segments*, one entry per note in every
field, made here from `voxy.score` notes by `soulx_metadata`:

> {“index”: “target_0”, “language”: “English”, “time”: [0, 6080],
> : “duration”: “0.30 0.60 …”, “text”: “<SP> Light a candle candle …”,
>   “phoneme”: “”, “note_pitch”: “0 64 64 67 …”, “note_type”: “1 2 2 3 …”, “f0”: “”}

`note_type` is 1 for a rest (`<SP>`), 2 where a word starts, 3 where it
continues; a word sung over several notes is written on each. Phonemes are left
empty and filled in the worker (English, g2p_en), so the host needs no phonemizer.
A synthesis prompt needs the same metadata, aligned to its clip
(`soulx_prompt_metadata`).

Usage disclaimer (upstream README; not a licence term): do not use the model to
impersonate anyone without authorisation or to create deceptive audio; respect
intellectual property, privacy and personal consent.

```pycon
>>> from voxy.score import Note
>>> meta = soulx_metadata([Note(0.0, 0.5, 64, "hel"), Note(0.5, 0.5, 67, "hel", False)])
>>> meta[0]["text"], meta[0]["note_type"], meta[0]["duration"]
('<SP> hel hel <SP>', '1 2 3 1', '0.30 0.50 0.50 0.40')
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_LEAD_S`](_autosummary/voxy.soulx.html.md#voxy.soulx.DFLT_LEAD_S)        | Rest before the first note and after the last (upstream's examples start with <SP>).                  |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_MIN_REST_S`](_autosummary/voxy.soulx.html.md#voxy.soulx.DFLT_MIN_REST_S)    | A gap shorter than this joins the previous note (legato); a longer one is a rest.                     |
| [`DFLT_SPLIT_REST_S`](_autosummary/voxy.soulx.html.md#voxy.soulx.DFLT_SPLIT_REST_S)  | A rest longer than this ends a segment.                                                               |
| [`DFLT_MAX_SEGMENT_S`](_autosummary/voxy.soulx.html.md#voxy.soulx.DFLT_MAX_SEGMENT_S) | No segment longer than this (upstream allows 60 s; shorter is safer on MPS).                          |
| [`SOULX_ENV`](_autosummary/voxy.soulx.html.md#voxy.soulx.SOULX_ENV)          | Upstream's inference pins (its requirements.txt minus the preprocessing, web UI and training stacks). |

### Functions

so a long song would change key between segments; voxy computes it once.

# _autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md

# voxy.speakers

Keep one speaker: find their voice in a recording and mark everyone else’s words.

Recordings of a person are rarely just that person: an interviewer asks the
questions, someone says “yes” or “uh-huh” in the middle of an answer. A clone or a
fine-tune trained on those clips learns the other voices too. This module
compares the voice in short sliding windows with a **voice print** (the mean
ECAPA speaker embedding of the target) and marks every transcribed word, and
every untranscribed stretch of someone else’s voice, that does not match it:

```pycon
>>> from voxy import refprep, speakers
>>> print_ = speakers.voice_print("clean_answer.wav")
>>> refprep.prepare_reference(["interview.m4a"], voice="ada",
...                           speaker=speakers.speaker_filter(print_))
```

`plan_clips` then never puts a marked word, or the pause around one, inside a
clip. With no voice print, `speaker_filter()` takes each recording’s
**dominant** voice (an iterated centroid over its loud windows), which is right
for a talk or an interview where the target does most of the talking.

The embeddings come from SpeechBrain’s ECAPA-TDNN (Apache-2.0, VoxCeleb weights)
running in voxy’s isolated `speaker` environment (`SPEAKER_ENV`, built on
first use, see `voxy.envs`); everything after the embeddings is numpy, so the
logic below is testable with made-up vectors.

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY)    | Cosine similarity to the voice print below which a window is someone else.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_SILENCE_MARGIN_DB`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_SILENCE_MARGIN_DB)   | neither voice.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [`DFLT_MIN_FOREIGN_SECONDS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_FOREIGN_SECONDS) | Untranscribed foreign stretches shorter than this are ignored (one window's wobble).                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`DFLT_FOREIGN_PAD_SECONDS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_FOREIGN_PAD_SECONDS) | Margin added around a foreign stretch, so a cut never clips its edge into a clip.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`DFLT_WORD_OVERLAP`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_WORD_OVERLAP)        | A word with this share of its length inside a foreign stretch is not kept.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`DFLT_DIP_SIMILARITY`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_DIP_SIMILARITY)      | Inside a transcribed turn, a stretch is someone else's only below this (smoothed) match: one-second windows of old, noisy audio dip well below `DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY` on the target's own voice, so a turn that matches as a whole is only cut where the dip is deep. |
| [`DFLT_SMOOTH_WINDOWS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_SMOOTH_WINDOWS)      | Window similarities are averaged over this many neighbours before finding stretches.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`DFLT_MIN_TURN_SECONDS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_TURN_SECONDS)    | never kept.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

### Functions

| [`close_speaker`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.close_speaker)()                                   | Stop the embedding workers (free their memory).                                       |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`dominant_centroid`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.dominant_centroid)(vectors, \*[, iterations, ...]) | The voice heard most: re-centre on the windows most like the centroid, repeatedly.    |
| [`embed_windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.embed_windows)(audio, \*[, spans, window, ...])    | ECAPA embeddings of `window`-second windows every `hop` s of `audio`.                 |
| [`foreign_spans`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.foreign_spans)(windows, similarity, \*[, ...])     | Stretches where a loud window does not match the voice print, padded by `pad`.        |
| [`loud_mask`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.loud_mask)(windows, samples, sample_rate, \*)      | Windows with speech in them: loud frames within `margin_db` of the speech level.      |
| [`mark_speaker`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.mark_speaker)(segments, windows, similarity, \*)   | Annotate each timed word with `speaker_similarity` and `keep`; add gap markers.       |
| [`smooth`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.smooth)(similarity[, windows])                     | Moving average of `similarity` over `windows` neighbours (edges: the shorter mean).   |

| [`turn_similarity`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.turn_similarity)(segments, windows, ...[, loud])   | Match of each transcribed segment (a turn) to `voice_print`, from its mean window.    |
| [`voice_print`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.voice_print)(audio, \*[, spans, embed])            | The voice print of `audio` (one recording or several): the dominant voice's centroid. |

### Classes

| [`Windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.Windows)(times, vectors)   | Speaker embeddings of sliding windows: `times` (n, 2) seconds, unit `vectors` (n, d).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_DIP_SIMILARITY *= 0.15*

Inside a transcribed turn, a stretch is someone else’s only below this (smoothed) match:
one-second windows of old, noisy audio dip well below `DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY` on the
target’s own voice, so a turn that matches as a whole is only cut where the dip is deep.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_FOREIGN_PAD_SECONDS *= 0.15*

Margin added around a foreign stretch, so a cut never clips its edge into a clip.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY *= 0.45*

Cosine similarity to the voice print below which a window is someone else.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_FOREIGN_SECONDS *= 0.2*

Untranscribed foreign stretches shorter than this are ignored (one window’s wobble).

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_TURN_SECONDS *= 1.0*

never kept.

* **Type:**
  Turns shorter than this are too short to attribute (”Yes.”, ”Uh-huh”)

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_SILENCE_MARGIN_DB *= 25.0*

neither voice.

* **Type:**
  Windows this far below the recording’s speech level are silence

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_SMOOTH_WINDOWS *= 3*

Window similarities are averaged over this many neighbours before finding stretches.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_WORD_OVERLAP *= 0.25*

A word with this share of its length inside a foreign stretch is not kept.

### *class* voxy.speakers.Windows(times, vectors)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Speaker embeddings of sliding windows: `times` (n, 2) seconds, unit `vectors` (n, d).

#### similarity(voice_print)

Cosine similarity of each window to `voice_print`.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.close_speaker()

Stop the embedding workers (free their memory).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### voxy.speakers.dominant_centroid(vectors, , iterations=6, quantile=0.5)

The voice heard most: re-centre on the windows most like the centroid, repeatedly.

Clustering fragments a noisy voice into several clusters; this converges on
the majority voice instead (it needs that voice to be more than half the windows
the first mean is computed from).

```pycon
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
>>> a, b = np.eye(4)[0], np.eye(4)[1]
>>> vs = np.array([_unit(a + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(4)) for _ in range(30)]
...             + [_unit(b + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(4)) for _ in range(10)])
>>> bool(dominant_centroid(vs) @ a > 0.95)
True
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.embed_windows(audio, , spans=None, window=1.0, hop=0.1, model='speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb', threads=None, rootdir=None)

ECAPA embeddings of `window`-second windows every `hop` s of `audio`.

`spans` restricts the windows to those `(start, end)` stretches (default:
the whole file). Any sample rate; the worker resamples to 16 kHz.

* **Return type:**
  [`Windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.Windows)

### voxy.speakers.foreign_spans(windows, similarity, , threshold=0.45, loud=None, min_seconds=0.2, pad=0.15)

Stretches where a loud window does not match the voice print, padded by `pad`.

`threshold` is one similarity, or one per window.

Each window speaks for the `hop`-wide slot around its centre, so a short “yes”
marks about the length of the dip it causes, not a whole window.

```pycon
>>> t = np.array([[i * 0.1, i * 0.1 + 1] for i in range(20)])
>>> sim = np.array([0.8] * 8 + [0.1] * 4 + [0.8] * 8)
>>> [[round(x, 2) for x in s] for s in foreign_spans(Windows(t, None), sim, pad=0)]
[[1.25, 1.65]]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]

### voxy.speakers.loud_mask(windows, samples, sample_rate, , margin_db=25.0)

Windows with speech in them: loud frames within `margin_db` of the speech level.

```pycon
>>> w = Windows(np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), np.zeros((2, 3)))
>>> x = np.concatenate([0.3 * np.ones(8000), np.zeros(8000)])
>>> loud_mask(w, x, 8000).tolist()
[True, False]
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.mark_speaker(segments, windows, similarity, , threshold=0.45, loud=None, turns=None, dip_threshold=0.15, min_turn_seconds=1.0, word_overlap=0.25, pad=0.15, min_seconds=0.2)

Annotate each timed word with `speaker_similarity` and `keep`; add gap markers.

Without `turns`, a word is kept when the windows centred inside it match the
voice print on average. With `turns` (one match per segment, see
[`turn_similarity()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.turn_similarity)), a word is kept when its whole segment matches and lasts
at least `min_turn_seconds`, and its `speaker_similarity` is the segment’s;
inside a segment only a deep dip (below `dip_threshold`) counts as someone else,
and a one-word sentence (“Yes.”) must match the voice print on its own.
Either way a word is dropped when `word_overlap` of it lies in a foreign
stretch. Every foreign stretch is also added as an empty word with
`keep=False` (an untranscribed “uh-huh” has no word of its own), padded by up
to `pad` and trimmed back to the kept words around it, so `refprep.plan_clips`
never puts it inside a clip. A segment without word timings is judged as one word.

```pycon
>>> t = np.array([[i * 0.1, i * 0.1 + 1] for i in range(40)])
>>> sim = np.array([0.8] * 15 + [0.1] * 5 + [0.8] * 20)
>>> w = lambda s, e, x: {"start": s, "end": e, "text": x}
>>> segs = [{"start": 0, "end": 4, "text": "a b",
...          "words": [w(0.5, 1.4, " a"), w(2.5, 3.8, " b")]}]
>>> out = mark_speaker(segs, Windows(t, None), sim)
>>> [(x["text"], x["keep"]) for x in out[0]["words"]], out[1]["words"][0]["end"]
([(' a', True), (' b', True)], 2.5)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.speakers.smooth(similarity, windows=3)

Moving average of `similarity` over `windows` neighbours (edges: the shorter mean).

```pycon
>>> smooth(np.array([1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0])).round(2).tolist()
[1.0, 0.67, 0.67, 0.67, 1.0]
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.speaker_filter(target=None, , threshold=0.45, dip_threshold=0.15, smooth_windows=3, min_turn_seconds=1.0, embed=None, \*\*embed_kwargs)

A `refprep.prepare_reference(speaker=...)` step: `(wav_path, segments) -> segments`.

Decides per transcribed segment (a turn: [`turn_similarity()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.turn_similarity)), then cuts
deep dips inside kept turns and other voices between them ([`mark_speaker()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.mark_speaker)).

* **Parameters:**
  * **target** (`ndarray` | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The voice print to keep (from [`voice_print()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.voice_print)); None takes each
    recording’s dominant voice.
  * **threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Cosine similarity a turn (or a stretch between turns) needs to
    count as the target.
  * **dip_threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Smoothed similarity below which a stretch inside a kept turn
    is someone else.
  * **smooth_windows** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Neighbouring windows averaged before finding stretches.
  * **min_turn_seconds** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Shorter turns are never kept.
  * **embed** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.Windows)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(path, **embed_kwargs) -> Windows` (default [`embed_windows()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.embed_windows)).
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]]

### voxy.speakers.turn_similarity(segments, windows, voice_print, , loud=None)

Match of each transcribed segment (a turn) to `voice_print`, from its mean window.

Averaging the embeddings over a whole turn is far steadier than any one window
on noisy audio: it is what tells an interviewer’s question from an answer. None
for a segment with no (loud) window centred in it.

```pycon
>>> t = np.array([[i * 0.1, i * 0.1 + 1] for i in range(40)])
>>> v = np.array([np.eye(2)[0]] * 20 + [np.eye(2)[1]] * 20)
>>> turn_similarity([{"start": 0, "end": 2}, {"start": 2.6, "end": 4.4}],
...                 Windows(t, v), np.eye(2)[0])
[1.0, 0.0]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

### voxy.speakers.voice_print(audio, , spans=None, embed=None, \*\*embed_kwargs)

The voice print of `audio` (one recording or several): the dominant voice’s centroid.

Pass recordings (or `spans` of one) where the target speaks alone, and this is
simply their voice; over mixed recordings it is whoever speaks most.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`


# _autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md

# voxy.speechtext

Display text vs speech text, and spotting words a model may misread.

A text a person reads and the text a model should be given are not always the same.
Measured case (French, a Qwen3-TTS clone): a verse line starting with a capitalised
verb, “Est parti” after a line “Mon frere”, was read as the noun /est/ (“l’Est”) in 4
of 4 takes; lowercased (“est parti”) it was read correctly in 4 of 4. The capital, not
the line break, is the trigger: line-initial “Est” tokenises like the noun in “l’Est”.
ASR checks cannot catch this (Whisper hears “est” either way), so the fix is upstream:

1. [`prepare_speech_text()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.prepare_speech_text) turns display text into speech text: it lowercases a
   *verse-initial* capital that does not start a sentence (keeping deliberate capitals:
   words also capitalised mid-line, or named in `keep`), then applies a per-language
   respelling table and proper-name aliases, and returns every change it made.
2. [`flag_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.flag_risks) lists the words of a text a model may misread (heteronyms you
   supply, e.g. from Lexique; more detectors plug in through `extra`), saying which
   ones sit where the capital trigger bites. [`pos_detector()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.pos_detector) is one such
   detector: it tags the text and, for heteronyms whose part of speech picks the
   reading (French “est”: verb /ɛ/, noun /ɛst/), names the `expected` reading;
   [`llm_detector()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.llm_detector) asks a language model for the risky words and their readings.

Engines differ in what they accept: for several local models text is the only lever
(they take no phonemes or SSML), so this is a text-level step; it plugs into
`LocalCloneSpeechModel(text_prep=...)`. Verifying the audio itself (phoneme
recognition of the flagged words) is [`voxy.pronounce`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#module-voxy.pronounce).

```pycon
>>> text = "Mon frere\nEst parti\nLoin d'ici."
>>> prepare_speech_text(text).speech
"Mon frere\nest parti\nloin d'ici."
>>> prepare_speech_text(text, keep={"Est", "Loin"}).speech == text
True
```

### voxy.speechtext.LLM_RISK_PROMPT *= 'You help a text-to-speech system avoid misreadings. Below is a $language text, its lines numbered. List the words a speech model may misread: heteronyms (words with more than one pronunciation, such as French "est" as a verb or as a noun), names, abbreviations. For each, give the line, the word exactly as written, short names of its possible readings, and the reading this context needs.\\n\\nAnswer with a JSON list only, one object per word:\\n[{"line": 2, "word": "est", "readings": ["verb", "noun"], "expected": "verb", "why": "..."}]\\nUse "expected": null when the context does not decide. Answer [] if nothing is risky.\\n\\n$text\\n'*

The prompt [`llm_detector()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.llm_detector) sends; `$language` and `$text` are filled in.

### voxy.speechtext.NOUN_CLITICS *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]]* *= {'fr': ("l'", "d'")}*

those that can come
before its noun reading (“l’Est”, “vent d’est”). After the others (“c’est”, “s’est”,
“n’est”) only the verb fits, and flagging every “c’est” would swamp a French text.

* **Type:**
  Clitics after which a heteronym is still flagged, by language

```pycon
>>> elided_words("Il est à l’Est", ("l'",))
```
